newsitem.title: USA: Living Centers, GranCare amend merger terms.
newsitem.headline: Living Centers, GranCare amend merger terms.

text.p: Living Centers of America Inc said on Monday that it and GranCare Inc have amended the terms of their proposed merger.
Under the amended terms, 10 percent of GranCare's shares are to be cancelled in exchange for $10 per share in cash, Living Centers said in a news release.
The other 90 percent of GranCare's outstanding shares were to be exchanged at the previously-announced ratio of 0.2469 of a Living Center share for each GranCare share.

The additonal cash to finance the GranCare cash option was to be provided by Apollo Management LP, which was to increase the amount of its investment in Living Centers to $228 million from $200 million.
As previously announced, Living Centers were to receive $40.50 per share for 93 percent of its outstanding shares, retaining seven percent.
The deal would leave Apollo owning 45 percent of Living Centers stock, current Living Centers holders with 43 percent and current GranCare shareholders with 12 percent.
The board of the combined company was to comprise six Apollo designees, three GranCare designees and one Living Center designee.

Edward Kuntz, Living Centers' chairman/chief executive, was to serve as president and chief executive of the combined firm. Scott Athans, GranCare's chief executive, was to be chief operating officer.
The combined firm was to be headquartered in Atlanta, where GranCare is based.
Living Centers provides health care services to senior citizens. GranCare provides specialty medical services and long-term care.
